title: Review: exponential and tanh shortcuts discard directed rounding outcomes
description:
Asymptotic shortcuts replace a strict mathematical limit by exact zero or one before applying the requested rounding direction. softfloat/trans.h:88 returns exact zero for large negative exp arguments; :200 returns exact +/-1 for large finite tanh inputs; :220 then incorrectly declares an underflowed exp2 result exact. On both published LLVM majors, exp_f64_rm(-100000,2) returns carrier0 flags24, but must return carrier1 (least positive subnormal) flags24. exp2_f64_rm(-100000,2) returns carrier0 flags0 rather than carrier1 flags24. tanh_f64_rm(256,1) returns 0x3ff0000000000000 flags16 rather than 0x3fefffffffffffff flags16. R=2 means upward; R=1 downward. Proof: e>2 gives 0<exp(-100000)<2^-100000<2^-1075; exp2(-100000)=2^-100000. Also tanh(256)=1-2/(exp(512)+1) lies strictly between 1-2^-511 and1. These violate the directed-side and final IEEE-flag obligations in published dialect section13.4; they are implementation bugs within bennett-arith-wvh, not missing contracts.

title: PPC exp loses sparse low components at tiny positive arguments
description: Both LLVM majors violate the 0.2.12 section 13.4 one-local-ulp bound for PPC exp at exact x=2^-700. Native constrained modes 0,1,3,4 return (1,+0); upward returns (1,2^-105), flags16. Exact series bounds for 0<x<1/2 give 1+x<exp(x)<1+x+x*x. The adjacent canonical pairs bracketing exp(x) are L=(1,2^-700), U=(1,2^-700+2^-752): both canonical and binary64 low components adjacent; other high bins are far away. Because x*x < (U-L)/2, nearest/down/towardzero must select L, upward U. Returning 1 has error greater than x, i.e. greater than 2^52 local ulps; returning 1+2^-105 is still farther. This is a full-domain numerical implementation bug, not a contract ambiguity. Add an independent exact-bound diagnostic witness and retain wvh pending full-domain repair/evidence; do not narrow source precision, reject inputs, weaken tests, or claim measured MPFR sweeps establish the envelope.
design: For valid canonical x=h+l, 0<|x|<=2^-112 implies exp(x)=1+z with RN64(1+any selected low)=1. Taylor gives0<z-x<x². Let2^E<=|h|<2^(E+1). Canonical nonoverlap gives|x|<2|h|; hence z-x<2^-111|h|<2^(E-110). A nonzero gap from h+l to a neighbouring binary64 midpoint is >=2^(E-107) (including the asymmetric power-of-two bin); subnormal half-grid gaps are larger. Thus nearest low rounding changes only at exact input midpoints, always upward. For directed modes, exp(x)-1>h iff x>log(1+h). Put h=M*2^e with at most53 significand bits, q=2^(2e-1). The logarithm residual is-h²/2+R, with sign(R)=sign(h), |R|<|h|³, and |h|³/q=2|h|M²<1/32. If negative l has exponent>=2e-1, any nonzero difference l+h²/2 is an integer multiple of q, so R cannot reverse it. If l has smaller exponent, h is normal and |l|<2^52*q while h²/2>=2^104*q, so the gap is much larger still. At exact quadratic equality, sign R settles the side: positive h selects below h, negative h above. Nonnegative l always selects above h. Compare h²/2 against |l| exactly at quantum2^-2149 in4352 bits. Directed output is the appropriate adjacent f64 field around h; nearest output is selected by exact midpoint distances. Zero gives exact1; nonzero rational x has transcendental exp(x), so final flags are inexact only. Total near1 excludes underflow/overflow/domain flags. Independent test oracle instead encloses z between x+x²/2+x³/6 and that plus x⁴ and requires both endpoints to round identically.
